lines: The app ships no composer/autoload.php, so the server registers its generic loader for lib/ and looks every class up in the file system.

A composer/composer.json with config.vendor-dir ".", config.optimize-autoloader true, a config.autoloader-suffix and autoload.psr-4 {"OCA\\SuspiciousLogin\\": "../lib/"} makes composer dump-autoload write composer/autoload.php with a class map; the code of the app does not change.
The Composer autoloader is optimized beyond level 1. The manual allows only config.optimize-autoloader: an authoritative class map breaks the upgrade of the app, and APCu is no required extension.
vendor/ ships 2 packages that the server ships itself in a major of Nextcloud 36. Both copies define the same classes, and the autoloader that is asked first decides which version runs.

lines: 2 uses in 2 files of the public API that is deprecated in Nextcloud 36. The text of the tag names the replacement where it has one.
lib/Listener/LoginMailListener.php:65 OCP\IConfig::getAppValue(): deprecated since Nextcloud 29; Use IAppConfig directly
lib/Notifications/Notifier.php:76 OCP\IConfig::getAppValue(): deprecated since Nextcloud 29; Use IAppConfig directly

3 transactions are opened and closed by hand. The trait TTransactional has atomic() since Nextcloud 24 and atomicRetry() since Nextcloud 27, which repeats a transaction that ran into a deadlock, as the manual recommends.

1 timed job does not say whether it is time sensitive. A job that sets TIME_INSENSITIVE with setTimeSensitivity() is moved to the maintenance window of the server; whether a job is heavy enough for that only its maintainer knows.
lib/ reads the clock directly in 5 places. OCP\AppFramework\Utility\ITimeFactory, a PSR-20 ClockInterface, gives the same time and can be replaced in a test.

The app reads and writes its app config in 2 places and registers no config lexicon, which IRegistrationContext::registerConfigLexicon() takes since Nextcloud 31. A lexicon states the type, the default and the sensitivity of each key in one place.
Nothing in the app calls 1 OCS route. OCS is there for clients outside the app, so this is no defect in itself.
The app has 1 OCS route and no openapi.json. Clients of OCS are generated from such a specification, and nothing else tells them what these routes take and return.
